awaiting_metrics.description: How many rows `analyze` would recompute right now — a lower bound, since a pass can re-invalidate rows as it runs. Shares Analyze.pending_metrics_count! with `plan`'s activities_awaiting_metrics, so the two commands cannot disagree, and it is the same predicate `analyze` selects on — beyond rows never scored it counts a changed FTP, a changed threshold pace, changed zones, a bumped metrics_rev, or any stored input column moving. Meaningless unless awaiting_metrics_known is true.

awaiting_metrics_known.description: False when the count could not be computed at all, in which case awaiting_metrics is 0 and must NOT be read as "nothing to do". config_error says why.

config_error.description: Why awaiting_metrics could not be computed, or "" when it could. Three conditions block it: the global HR zones absent, a global zone key unparseable, or a per-sport override unparseable. `doctor` degrades on all three and reports the reason, because a command that exists to diagnose a broken installation must not die on what it is diagnosing. `plan` survives only the third — it propagates the other two and exits non-zero. `analyze` reports the same condition and is the command to run for the remedy.

unanalyzed.description: Activities with no metrics row at all — never scored. A COVERAGE number, matching its neighbours here, which all report what the data has rather than whether it is current. It is NOT what `analyze` would recompute: see awaiting_metrics, which is never smaller WHENEVER awaiting_metrics_known is true. When that flag is false this field can exceed it, because the other count is 0 and means nothing.

undateable_activities.description: Activities whose `start_local` cannot be read — NULL, empty, malformed, or a year before 1000. These are the rows that make `analyze`, `summary`, `season`, `plan`, `stats` and `week` refuse with `unreadable_activity_date`, and doctor reported a clean engine beside them until #265. A COUNT, not a verdict: the remedy is per-row, so `stride activities` lists them first and each is repaired by deleting it by id and re-syncing. Zero on a healthy database, and the human screen omits the line entirely at zero rather than printing a row the eye learns to skip.

unrankable_activities.description: How many activities the engine refuses a ranking position — exactly the rows published with `rankable: false`, and exactly the population `stride activities` hoists to the top as needing repair. Distinct from `undateable_activities`, which counts the rows with `date_known: false` and is a SUBSET: after #255 the hoist grew a time half and the count did not, so a row at the very top of the listing was reported as zero undateable (#282). Each count corresponds to one row flag, so the two can be cross-checked against the listing. A COUNT and not a verdict — ADR 0012 puts 'is this a problem?' on the coach's side.
